t: Maximum Sum of M Non-Overlapping Subarrays — Prefix Sums + Monotonic Queue DP
o: We must pick between 1 and m disjoint contiguous pieces of `nums`, each piece having length in `[l, r]`, maximizing total sum. Example 1 shows two pieces ([4,1] and [2]) beating one piece; Example 4 shows that when everything is negative we still must pick at least one piece, so the answer can be negative. With n ≤ 1000 and m ≤ n, an O(n·m) DP fits easily, while a naive O(n·m·r) transition needs optimization.
k: Prefix sums turn any window sum into P[i] − P[t], letting the DP transition become P[i] + max over t of (dp[t] − P[t]).
The inner maximum over t ∈ [i−r, i−l] is a sliding-window maximum, solvable with a monotonic deque in amortized O(1).
"At most m" is handled for free by letting dp carry previous-layer values forward.

a.n: Approach 1: Layered DP with brute-force window scan
a.i: Let dp[j][i] be the best sum using at most j subarrays within the first i elements. Either we don't end a piece at i (dp[j][i−1]), or some piece of length len ∈ [l, r] ends at i, contributing dp[j−1][i−len] + P[i] − P[i−len]. Trying every length directly gives an easy-to-reason-about solution.
s: For each count j from 1 to m, compute dp[j][i] = max(dp[j][i−1], max over len of dp[j−1][i−len] + P[i] − P[i−len]).
Answer is the max of dp[m][*] (which already includes fewer pieces via the carry).
a.t: O(m · n · r) — three nested loops over count, position, and window length
a.sp: O(n) — two rolling DP rows plus prefix sums

a.i: Rewrite the transition as dp[j][i] = max(dp[j][i−1], P[i] + max_{t∈[i−r,i−l]}(dp[j−1][t] − P[t])). The bracketed term is a sliding-window maximum over t, maintained with a monotonic deque storing indices with decreasing dp[t] − P[t]. This removes the factor of r entirely.
s: For each layer j, sweep i from 0 to n; push t = i − l into the deque keeping dp[t] − P[t] decreasing, evict indices < i − r.
Transition uses the deque front; also carry dp[j][i] ≥ dp[j−1][i] for "at most m".
Track the global maximum over all layers ≥ 1 (at least one piece required).
a.t: O(n·m) — each index enters and leaves the deque once per layer
a.sp: O(n) — prefix sums, two DP rows, deque

w: Lead with the layered DP formulation, then optimize the window-max transition with the deque — interviewers expect both steps. Pitfalls: forgetting the "at least one subarray" requirement (answer can be negative, e.g. Example 4), off-by-one on window bounds [i−r, i−l], and 64-bit sums since values reach 1e9. Follow-ups: what if pieces had to be exactly length l (trivially simpler), or if at least m pieces were required (change the carry rule).
